newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Bolivia's Vinto says tin smelter strike over.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia's Vinto says tin smelter strike over.

text.p: Bolivia's state-owned Vinto tin smelter has been working normally since Friday, when striking workers and management reached a deal on payment of a special bonus, the company and union officials said Monday.
"Operations were normalized last Friday night," Empresa Metalurgica general manager Rene Candia told Reuters by telephone from La Paz.

He said the strike began last Monday over a dispute over the payment of a 1995 productivity bonus. The company initially said production targets had not been met and would not pay, but changed its position during the strike.
"The company executives and the government have decided to make them an extraordinary payment equivalent to 45 percent of the bonus, to avoid damage to the company," Candia said.
He said comments by unionists in La Paz last week that the strike began after the company informed half the 1,000 strong workforce that they were to lose their jobs were wrong.
"That is completely false. The company has not issued employment termination papers to any worker," he said.
A local representative of Bolivia's labor federation (COB) for the Vinto area confirmed to Reuters that the strike was over after a deal was reached on bonus payments.
Candia said the smelter had been almost completely shut and production lost over the five-day strike, but a skeleton workforce had kept some equipment operating to avoid damage.
COB official David Rojas also confirmed that the Vinto workers had not been issued with dismissal papers, but said that the company had threatened to sack workers if they did not accept a deal.

Rojas added that management said it would only make the extraordinary payment if workers dropped their opposition to the government's planned privatization of the smelter, saying the company's general manager wanted to blackmail the workers.
Vinto is slated for privatization in January but has recently suffered protests and stoppages by the workforce.

Four companies have been short-listed to bid in Vinto's privatization tender: Glencore International of Switzerland; Australia's Renison Goldfields Consolidated; Smelting Corp Berhad of Malaysia, and Brazil's Paranapanema.
Apart from its Bolivian suppliers, Peru's Minsur also provides tin concentrates for tolling into metal at Vinto.
Vinto's 1996 output was forecast, before the strike, to be almost 18,000 tonnes of tin. The smelter also produces 4,500 to 5,000 tonnes a year of antimony.
